<description>
Follow-up to #36340, addressing the review comments from pinheadmz and winterrdog there.

#36340 capped the `Sock::Wait`/`WaitMany` timeout at `INT_MAX` milliseconds (about 24.8 days) inside `WaitMany`. This moves that value to a named constant, `Sock::MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT`, and mentions the cap in the doxygen comments of `Wait()` and `WaitMany()`, since it applies to every caller and not only to `bitcoin-cli`. The constant is a whole number of seconds (2147483 s), so `bitcoin-cli`, which works in seconds, uses exactly the same value as `Sock`.

`bitcoin-cli` still turned `-rpcclienttimeout=0` into a 5 year timeout. The timeout is applied to each wait for the socket, and each wait is now capped, so in practice `0` already means "give up after about 24.8 days without data". The 5 year value is replaced with `Sock::MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT`, and the help text now says that 0 is the longest supported timeout (about 24 days) instead of no timeout.

There is no behaviour change. `sock_tests`, `interface_bitcoin_cli.py` (including the `-rpcclienttimeout=0` call added in #36340) and `interface_rpc.py` pass on macOS.

(Changes prepared with AI tools.)
</description>
